candidates.name: Abu Safa Field Crude Trunkline

values.RouteNotes: No official GIS/route map found. Sources confirm only the offshore Abu Safa field as origin and a ~50km, 42-in EPCI scope; the onshore terminus/receiving facility is not named in any source found, so EndLocation is left blank per dataset convention (cf. other Saudi rows with unresolved endpoints, e.g. P1987, P1958).

candidates.researcher_notes:
New Aramco EPCI (Saipem) crude trunkline for the offshore Abu Safa (Abu Safah) field, shared 50/50 reservoir with Bahrain: 42-in diameter, ~50km, awarded July 15-16 2024 under Saipem's Aramco long-term agreement, part of a combined ~$500m two-project award. Meets all three add-threshold legs: sponsor (Saudi Aramco, Saipem as EPCI contractor), country+region (Saudi Arabia, offshore Abu Safa field in the Gulf near the Bahrain maritime border), and concrete step (signed EPCI contract award, not just rumor). Re-checked against the 50 existing Saudi Arabia rows myself: no row names Abu Safa; nearest namesake is P0637 'Bahrain Saudi Arabia Oil Pipeline' (AB-4), which is a distinct, already-operating Abqaiq->Bapco Refinery product line unrelated to this new field-gathering trunkline, so this is correctly a new row, not a match.

Corroboration: primary is Saipem's own press release; independently confirmed (matching diameter/length/contract type/date, not just a verbatim reprint) by World Pipelines (added field production-capacity and reserve context absent from the Saipem release), epcintel.com, and Ghana Upstream. Several other hits (SA World, Storage Terminals Mag, Tank News International, Energy Pedia, Saudi Gulf Projects, World Ports) are near-verbatim syndications of the same Saipem release and were not used as independent refs.

Caveats / things deliberately left blank rather than guessed:
- The consolidator's parenthetical '(CRPO 138)' contract-package tag could NOT be found in the text of any of the four fetched sources (checked via raw-text grep, not just the AI summaries) -- dropped from the row name rather than risk citing an unverified/possibly fabricated identifier.
- World Pipelines' '300,000 bpd' figure is explicitly the Abu Safa FIELD's total production capacity (split 50/50 Bahrain/Saudi), not a stated throughput rating for this specific trunkline -- left Capacity blank rather than misattribute field output to the pipe.
- The ~$500m contract value is a COMBINED figure covering this trunkline plus a separate, unrelated Berri/Manifa fields production-maintenance award in the same press release -- cost could not be isolated to just this pipeline, so ProjectLevelCost was left blank.
- No post-July-2024 news of progress, delay, or completion was found (search budget for this session was exhausted mid-task; supplemented with DuckDuckGo HTML fetches once WebSearch was unavailable). Set Status='construction' from the confirmed EPCI award with no evidence of stoppage; ~2 years elapsed is unremarkable for an offshore trunkline of this scope, not treated as a dormancy signal.
- EndLocation/EndCountryOrArea left blank (not '?') because no source names the onshore receiving facility -- follows the existing dataset's own convention of blank-for-unknown rather than a placeholder string.
- CountriesOrAreas scoped to Saudi Arabia only: no source indicates this specific trunkline crosses into Bahrain (Bahrain's share of Abu Safa crude already moves via the existing operating P0637/AB-4 line); this new line reads as Aramco's own within-Saudi-Arabia gathering/export infrastructure for the field.
- RouteAccuracy='no route' / RouteType='Unavailable (cannot find route)': no official GIS, and the only named point is the offshore field itself, not a two-endpoint corridor.

candidates.name: Berri Downstream Pipeline (Abu Ali Island-Khursaniyah-Ju'aymah)

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: Two new lines (30-in stabilized Arabian Light crude + 10-in sour condensate) built 2019-2023 from Aramco's Abu Ali Island processing plant/GOSP to the existing Khursaniyah Gas Plant and Ju'aymah tank farm, installed 'via expanding the existing KRT [Khursaniyah-Ras Tanura] pipeline corridor' (Saipem). Endpoints only -- no traced geometry or total route km found in open sources. Saipem quotes an offshore 'pulling length of over 8 km' for four pipe sections, but that figure is explicitly the marine shore-pull/pipelay crossing (Abu Ali Island landfall), not the full onshore-to-Khursaniyah/Ju'aymah route length, so it is NOT used as LengthKnown. Source does not state which of the two pipes (30-in crude vs 10-in condensate) terminates at which of the two endpoints (Khursaniyah Gas Plant vs Ju'aymah tank farm) -- both endpoints are listed together in the single EndLocation value above rather than paired to a specific diameter, to avoid asserting an unconfirmed pairing.
values.Background: Part of Saudi Aramco's Berri Increment Program, which adds facilities (new GOSP at Abu Ali Island, expanded gas processing at Khursaniyah, water injection, offshore platforms/drilling islands) to raise Berri field crude availability by ~250,000 bpd (250 MBCD) of Arabian Light crude plus associated condensate handling. These two downstream pipelines were built to carry that increment from Abu Ali Island onward to existing Khursaniyah/Ju'aymah infrastructure.

candidates.researcher_notes: RE-CHECK vs existing rows done first: full-CSV grep for 'Berri'/'Abu Ali'/'Khursaniyah'/'Kursaniyah'/'Juaymah' across all Saudi Arabia GOIT rows turns up P1970 (Abu Ali-Berri junction), P1978 (Berri junction-Ras Tanura), the Khursaniyah-Ras Tanura/KRT family (P1963/1967/1968/5159), the Safiniyah-Kursaniyah family (P1964/1965/1966/5169), Qatif Junction-Juaymah (P1987/1988/1989) and Safaniyah-Juaymah (P1958) -- none of these start at Abu Ali Island itself and run to Khursaniyah Gas Plant/Ju'aymah tank farm; they are all different corridors (Berri junction, Safiniyah, Qatif Junction, Safaniyah as the other endpoint), confirming the consolidator note that this is genuinely new construction, not a rename/duplicate of P1970/P1978 or the KRT family. Class = new_row. Add-threshold: (a) sponsor -- Saudi Aramco, confirmed by Saipem (client) and independently by nsenergybusiness (Aramco awarded the EPIC contracts); Aramco is an existing entity (entity_lookup.py exact match 'Saudi Aramco', no new entity needed); (b) country+endpoints -- Saudi Arabia, Abu Ali Island processing plant to Khursaniyah Gas Plant and Ju'aymah tank farm, stated directly by Saipem and corroborated (facility locations, not pipeline detail) by Sadeen Group/GCS's subcontract scope 'at Saudi Aramco's existing plants, Khursaniyah and Abu Ali, under the Berri increment program'; (c) concrete step -- EPIC contract award (Saudi Aramco awarded ~$1.3bn EPIC contracts to Saipem in July 2019 as part of 34 contracts/$18bn across the Marjan and Berri increment programs, per nsenergybusiness) followed by completed construction (Saipem: 'When 2019-2023'). All three legs clear. Independent=true: three separately-run sites (Saipem's own corporate project page as primary/contractor source; NS Energy Business, an independent energy trade-press outlet, on the 2019 contract award; Sadeen Group/GCS, an independent Saudi subcontractor, on its Khursaniyah/Abu Ali civil-works scope) agree on sponsor, program and locations -- not one wire story reprinted. Tier=medium: the engineering specifics (30-in/10-in diameters, the two-endpoint routing, the 2019-2023 build window) come from a single primary source (Saipem, the EPC contractor -- a company/project-page source, so filled at medium/yellow per the single-strong-source rule rather than left blank), with the broader program/location/sponsor facts independently corroborated by nsenergybusiness and Sadeen Group. No confirmed total pipeline length was found (the Saipem '8 km' figure is only the offshore shore-pull crossing, not end-to-end) and no route geometry exists, so RouteAccuracy=low/endpoints-only and LengthKnown is left blank rather than guessed. Capacity (250,000 bpd) is the Berri field crude-increment figure the pipelines were purpose-built to carry per Saipem/nsenergybusiness, used as the best available capacity proxy since no separate pipeline-only throughput rating was published -- flagged here as a proxy, not an independently verified nameplate figure. ProjectLevelCost intentionally left blank: the only cost figures found ($1.3bn Saipem EPIC award, $18bn combined Marjan+Berri total) cover contract scope well beyond just these two pipelines, so attributing either number to this pipeline alone would misstate cost.

candidates.name: Safaniya Offshore-Onshore Crude Trunkline (CRPO 156)

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: Start endpoint (Safaniya offshore oil field, Arabian Gulf, off Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province) is named in all three sources; the onshore terminus is described only generically as an onshore processing/receiving facility, not named. No GIS/shapefile route located. Corridor is ~65 km offshore + 12 km onshore (~77 km total) per Saipem's EPCI scope. Do not draw a route until the onshore endpoint is confirmed by name — flagged for a future route-research pass once more detail (e.g. FERC-style project map or Aramco filing) surfaces.

candidates.researcher_notes:
New-row: confirmed distinct from all existing Safaniya-area GEM rows. P1958 (Safaniyah-Juaymah Oil Pipeline, 198 km, 46/48-in) and P1964-P1966/P5169 (Safiniyah-Kursaniyah Oil Pipelines, 106 km, 22-48-in, 4 parallel lines) are both far longer than this candidate's ~77 km (65 km offshore + 12 km onshore) and none of the three evidence sources reference either existing line, a rebuild, or an upgrade of them — this is a new physical trunkline under a new EPCI award, not a renaming.

Sponsor/step/geography threshold (Discovery SOP §3): (a) sponsor = Saudi Aramco (client, existing Long-Term Agreement) with Saipem as EPCI contractor, both named in all 3 sources; (b) country + start endpoint = Saudi Arabia, Safaniya offshore oil field (Eastern Province/Arabian Gulf) — named specifically; onshore endpoint is only generically described, not named, so route/EndLocation are left unfilled; (c) concrete step = EPCI contract formally awarded Feb 23, 2026 (Saipem CRPO under its Aramco LTA). All three legs met -> new_row, not monitor.

CRPO project-code check: the candidate's proposed name carries a '(CRPO 156)' suffix from the consolidator note, but I read the full text of all three sources directly (not just the AI summary) looking for a numeric CRPO identifier and none states '156' or any other CRPO number — Saipem's own release calls it simply 'a Contract Release Purchase Order (CRPO)' with no number given. I dropped '(CRPO 156)' from the staged PipelineName since I can't verify that digit against any cited source (best not to carry an unconfirmed number into the tracker); flagging here in case the consolidator has a fourth source with the number that I don't have access to.

Corroboration/independence: Saipem's own press release (primary, company disclosure) states the core facts (48-in, 65 km offshore + 12 km onshore, Safaniya field, Aramco LTA, contract worth ~$500m per the page title) and is verified live. Offshore Engineer explicitly cites the Saipem release and adds no new facts (essentially a reprint) — flagging this so tier isn't overstated. JPT's piece, however, does add independently-reported context beyond the release: it cites Aramco CEO Amin Nasser's 2022 and 2024 remarks to Arab News about the Safaniya increment/expansion program and pulls figures from Aramco's Q3 2025 earnings report on other brownfield increment projects (Marjan, Berri, Zuluf, Dammam phase 2) — showing its own reporting/verification rather than pure republication. On balance this clears the '>=2 independent sources' bar, but since the core physical specs (length/diameter) trace to one origin (Saipem), and the $500m cost figure is stated only in Saipem's own release title (not repeated by either trade outlet), I'm scoring tier=medium rather than high.

Status call: set Status=construction (not proposed) because the CRPO is a signed/awarded EPCI contract, not merely an FID or planning milestone — Aramco/Saipem's LTA framework issues CRPOs as ready-to-execute work orders, and Saipem names its assigned fabrication yard, i.e. execution is mobilizing. FIDStatus left blank per the vocab rule (only populated when Status=proposed). If a QC pass judges the project not yet physically under way as of this writing, ConstructionYear/Month can be reclassified to Status=proposed + FIDStatus=FID with the same refs.

Owner: 'Saudi Aramco' matched via entity_lookup.py to existing entity ID 100 (oil tracker) — reuse, not a new entity; Parent left blank (not restated in these sources, and Owner already captures the identified sponsor).

Route: no official GIS route exists; RouteAccuracy=no route because the onshore terminus is unnamed in reporting (only 'onshore' is stated) so even a basic point-to-point line would be a guess — left for a dedicated route pass once the onshore facility is named.

candidates.name: Zuluf Field-Ju'aymah Crude Oil Pipeline(s)

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: Endpoints only (field CPF to Ju'aymah export terminal); no traced geometry or route km found in open sources. CRPO 79 tender describes two 42-in oil trunklines (east/west) plus a 42-in water-injection line running onshore+offshore from the Zuluf development to a beach valve station -- that spec covers the offshore-field-to-onshore-landfall leg. The separate onshore leg carrying stabilized crude on to Ju'aymah terminal is described in project-database write-ups without its own diameter/length, so the 42-in figure should be read as confirmed for the offshore/beach-valve segment, not verified end-to-end to Ju'aymah.

candidates.researcher_notes: RE-CHECK vs existing rows: none of the 50 existing Saudi Arabia GOIT oil rows name Zuluf or Tanajib, and none run field-to-Ju'aymah on this route (the two Juaymah-adjacent rows, P1958 Safaniyah-Juaymah and P1987/1988/1989 Qatif Junction-Juaymah, are different fields/corridors) -- genuinely new, not a rename/duplicate. Add-threshold: (a) sponsor Saudi Aramco confirmed independently by offshore-technology and nsenergybusiness -- Aramco already exists in the oil entity table (entity_lookup exact match, no new entity created); (b) endpoints Zuluf offshore field -> onshore CPF -> Ju'aymah crude terminal, Saudi Arabia, confirmed by nsenergybusiness + offshore-technology; (c) concrete step -- CRPO 79 EPC tender (metenders, Jan 2020: two 42-in oil trunklines east/west + 42-in water-injection line, onshore+offshore, beach valve station) and zawya's June 2024 update that the Zuluf crude-oil-increment project is in active EPC targeting ~2026 completion. All three legs clear -- new_row, Status=construction. Capacity 600,000 bpd is the Zuluf 'AH' crude increment the pipeline(s) are sized to carry (nsenergybusiness), used as the best available capacity proxy since no separate pipeline-only throughput figure was published. One caveat folded into RouteNotes: the CRPO 79 tender's 42-in trunkline spec plainly covers the offshore-field-to-beach-valve-station leg; the further onshore run from the CPF to Ju'aymah terminal is described qualitatively ('new downstream pipelines ... send stabilized crude to Ju'aymah') by nsenergybusiness/offshore-technology without its own diameter or length, so treat 42-in as confirmed for part of the route, not the full length. Also flagging a discovery-note accuracy issue: the queue evidence listed upstreamonline.com/.../2-1-1073114 as corroborating 'CRPO 79' via McDermott, but the fetched article text only discusses CRPOs 73, 74 and 84 (McDermott bidding) -- 'CRPO 79' does not appear in it; Zuluf shows up only via a linked related-story headline. That source was verified live (200 OK, 'Zuluf' present) but is NOT used as a ref here because it doesn't actually support the CRPO 79 claim -- excluded rather than cited. The remaining four sources (nsenergybusiness, offshore-technology, metenders, zawya) are independently published (project-database site, separate project-database site, tender-listing site, regional business-news wire) and mutually corroborate route/scope/status, so independent=true holds without the upstreamonline piece. Tier=medium: sponsor/route/status are solid and cross-corroborated, but no route geometry, no confirmed full-route length, and the diameter figure is segment-specific as noted above -- not solid enough for 'high'.
